text:
For forty minutes this looked like the night Edmonton finally got off the mat. Then Kaapo Kakko scored twice in two minutes, and the Oilers are now winless in five (0-4-1).

Seattle struck first on a shot that had no business going in. Jordan Eberle, back in the building where his career started, beat Tristan Jarry with a slap shot at 11:21 of the first, an 8% chance by our numbers. The Oilers took over from there. Connor McDavid, who came in with Yahoo Sports noting he could match Mark Messier's home scoring streak, tied it on a second-period power play from Evan Bouchard and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. Leon Draisaitl tipped in the go-ahead goal at 13:07, and Edmonton owned that period, 1.16 expected goals (the quality of chances, added up) to 0.60. Seattle also changed goalies along the way: Philipp Grubauer stopped 16 of 18, and Joey Daccord finished it with nine saves on nine shots.

The third belonged to the Kraken. Kakko's slap shot at 12:48 tied it, and his wrister at 14:48 put Seattle ahead, both set up by Matty Beniers. Neither was a great look (9% and 6%), and that is the sore spot for Edmonton: Jarry allowed about one goal more than his 31 shots deserved. Kakko played only 12:36 and added 0.72 wins by our count, easily the most of anyone. Vince Dunn closed it at 18:38.

On the whole, Edmonton probably deserved better. Our replays of every shot gave the Oilers the win 66% of the time, and they had eight power plays to Seattle's four, though one goal on 1.88 expected goals of power-play chances is its own problem. The Oilers also outhit Seattle 40 to 10, which says more about who had the puck than who was winning. Beniers' line kept answering. For a team with McDavid and Draisaitl both scoring, five games without a win is the kind of stretch that gets loud in Edmonton, and our numbers suggest the finishing and goaltending, not the effort, are what's missing.
headline: Kakko's two late goals push Oilers to five without a win
